## 1. One-paragraph verdict
Genuine MPEG-2 elementary stream, and every fact the test lane and the format record claim about it reproduces bit-accurately under independent tooling: sequence header 192x108 (bytes `00 00 01 b3 0c 00 6c` — 0x0C0=192, 0x06C=108), first sequence extension carries `profile_and_level_indication = 0x85` (the escaped 4:2:2 Profile @ Level 5 byte, bit-decoded by me: ((d[16]&0xF)<<4)|(d[17]>>4)), ffprobe reads profile `4:2:2`, level `5`, `yuv422p`, `25/1`, `field_order=progressive`, 15 frames (`nb_read_packets=15` == my picture-start-code count of 15). ffmpeg decodes it cleanly to raw yuv422p (md5 `3cba0873c6c5f2033f1aad224407b8a1`, zero errors). The consuming suite passed in baseline (3/3). `file(1)` misreports it as a Targa image — that is `file`'s magic weakness with MPEG start codes, not a fixture defect; ffprobe/python parsing are authoritative.

## 2. What actually works (verified)
- python3 bit parse: sequence_header_code 00 00 01 B3, h=192, v=108; B5 extension id=1 (sequence extension), profile_and_level_indication=0x85 — exactly the record's "escaped 4:2:2 0x85" claim (docs/formats/video-mpeg12.md:61,88; archive worklog row "4:2:2@5 (escaped 0x85)").
- ffprobe: codec_name=mpeg2video, profile=4:2:2, level=5, width=192, height=108, pix_fmt=yuv422p, r_frame_rate=25/1, field_order=progressive, nb_read_packets=15 — every field matches the lane tuple at mpeg12_corpus.rs:204-214 (192, 108, "4:2:2", Some(5), "yuv422p", "25/1", false-interlaced).
- `ffmpeg -i ... -f rawvideo -pix_fmt yuv422p - | md5sum` -> clean decode, `3cba0873c6c5f2033f1aad224407b8a1`.
- Baseline: cargo-test-workspace.txt:1281-1289 — mpeg12_corpus 3/3 ok (fixture facts asserted through the wired parser + ffprobe cross-check).
